summary: Kentucky gives the practice real, citeable teeth against fully insured commercial plans, self-insured governmental/church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and every Kentucky Medicaid MCO (KRS 205.593(2)) - but none against Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law) or self-funded ERISA plans such as UMR and UHC Shared Services (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144). Do they have to answer? Yes, in-scope payers must: pay, deny or contest a clean claim in 30 calendar days (304.17A-702), acknowledge e-claims in 48 hours and list every missing item at that time (704), contest only on four grounds (706), fix contracted-rate underpayments within 30 days without an appeal (708(1)), retro-deny only within 24 months of payment (708(3)), give 30 days to dispute overpayments and not recoup while a dispute is open (714), not seek overpayments more than 2 years after the claim was filed (304.14-375), decide internal appeals in 30 days (617) or face deemed exhaustion (619(2)), and treat a missed UR deadline as a deemed authorization (607(3)). Late clean claims carry 12/18/21% interest that must be added without asking and paid within 30 days of payment (730; 806 KAR 17:360). If they ignore the practice, a written DOI complaint forces an answer: the insurer must respond to DOI in 15 calendar days and the commissioner must make a finding (KRS 304.2-165); DOI may fine $1,000 per day or 10% of the unpaid claim per day (304.99-123, discretionary, only when quarterly 95%/90% compliance is missed), up to $10,000 per violation under the unfair claims practices act (304.12-230(16),(17); 304.99-020), and complaints count at license renewal. Medicaid MCOs add: free copies of all criteria, a 120-day appeal window with 30-day decisions and 30-day payment after a win (205.534), an in-person meeting once unpaid claims pass $2,500 in aggregate, no timely-filing denials of timely first claims, no audit recoupment before external review, and a binding external independent third-party review that can bundle many claims under one 'policy or practice' (205.646; 907 KAR 17:035/040) with loser-pays hearing fees and mandatory DMS enforcement (205.5356). Medigap carriers fall outside 17A but are bound by KRS 304.12-235 (30 days, 12%, attorney's fees for providers), 806 KAR 12:092 and 806 KAR 17:570 Sec. 15 (pay on the Medicare crossover). Not confirmed: provider standing to sue under the unfair claims act (KRS 446.070) and how DMS treats bundled external reviews.

rules.quote: "Insurer" means any insurance company; health maintenance organization; self-insurer, including a governmental plan, church plan, or multiple employer welfare arrangement, not exempt from state regulation by ERISA
rules.applies_to: Gate for every KRS 304.17A rule below. In: insurance companies, HMOs, nonprofit hospital/medical-surgical/health service corporations, self-insured governmental plans, church plans, non-exempt MEWAs, provider-sponsored networks. Out: self-funded ERISA employer plans; Medicare supplement, KRS Chapter 205 (Medicaid) coverage and other excepted benefits are excluded from 'health benefit plan' (304.17A-005(22)(b); 304.17A-008(2)(f),(k)), although Medicaid MCOs are pulled back into prompt pay by KRS 205.593(2).
rules.requires: Defines which payers are bound by Subtitle 17A (prompt pay, UR, appeals, external review).
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: If the plan is outside the definition, the Subtitle 17A rules (interest, 24-month limits, DOI fines) cannot be cited against it.
rules.provider_use: Before citing Kentucky law in a letter, classify the plan from the ID card/835 (fully insured vs ASO/self-funded, governmental, church, Medicaid MCO, MA). Use the Kentucky citations only for in-scope plans; for ASO/self-funded and MA claims use the federal ERISA/CMS rules instead.

rules.quote: Any fully insured health benefit plan or self-insured plan issued or renewed to public employees pursuant to this section shall comply with: ... KRS 304.17A-600 to 304.17A-633; (d) KRS 205.593; (e) KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730; (f) KRS 304.14-135; (g) KRS 304.17A-580 and 304.17A-641; (h) KRS 304.99-123;
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (Public Employee Health Insurance Program), fully insured or self-insured, including its claims administrator. Same text continues in the version effective 1/1/2027.
rules.requires: State employee plan must follow KY prompt pay, UR/internal appeal/external review statutes, uniform claim form rule, and the DOI prompt-pay fines statute.
rules.deadline: Same as the incorporated statutes (30 days to pay/deny etc.).
rules.consequence: All prompt-pay interest, 24-month limits and DOI fines apply even though the plan is self-insured.
rules.provider_use: Treat KEHP claims exactly like fully insured Kentucky claims in letters; cite KRS 18A.225(22) together with the specific 304.17A section so the administrator cannot answer that the plan is 'self-funded'.

rules.quote: each insurer shall reimburse a provider for a clean claim or send a written or an electronic notice denying or contesting the claim within thirty (30) calendar days from the date that the claim is received by the insurer or any entity that administers or processes claims on behalf of the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Pay the clean claim per the provider contract, or pay the undisputed part and give written/electronic reasons for the rest, or give written/electronic reasons that nothing will be paid.
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days from receipt by the insurer or its claims processor (60 days for organ transplants). 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 3(3): also compliant if paid within 3 business days of a check dated day 28-30.
rules.consequence: Interest under KRS 304.17A-730 (12%/18%/21% a year from the due date, added automatically); DOI may fine under KRS 304.99-123; repeated failure is also evidence for KRS 304.12-230(2),(5),(6).
rules.provider_use: Unanswered or pended claims older than 30 days: send a demand citing 702(1) and 730, state the received date (clearinghouse 999/277CA acceptance), the date payment was due (day 30) and the interest owed to date, and that a Health Care Provider Clean Claim Complaint will be filed with the Department of Insurance if not paid.

rules.quote: "Clean claim" means a properly completed billing instrument, paper or electronic, including the required health claim attachments
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Defines a clean claim; for physicians it is the HCFA 1500 data set or successor in the NUCC paper or electronic format (304.17A-700(3)(c)).
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: A claim meeting this definition starts the 30-day clock of 304.17A-702.
rules.provider_use: State in each letter that the claim was submitted on the 837P/CMS-1500 data set with all required attachments listed in the payer's provider manual, so it is a clean claim under 700(3).

rules.quote: shall notify the provider, its billing agent, or designee that submitted the claim, in writing or electronically, of all information that is missing from the billing instrument, any errors in the billing instrument, or of any other circumstances which preclude it from being a clean claim.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Acknowledge electronic claims within 48 hours and paper claims within 20 calendar days; at that time list every missing item/error; adjudicate the corrected clean claim within the 702 time frame; offer claim status on the remittance or electronically.
rules.deadline: 48 hours (electronic) or 20 calendar days (paper) from receipt; corrected clean claim then 30 days.
rules.consequence: A later request for information that was not flagged at acknowledgment undercuts any argument that the claim was not clean; interest and fines then run from day 30.
rules.provider_use: When a payer pends for information weeks later, cite 704(2): the defect had to be named at acknowledgment, so the claim was clean on receipt and interest runs from day 30.

rules.quote: Provide the date the claim was received by an insurer, its agent, or designee, an insurer reference number for the claim, and one (1) of the following dated actions
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). Also dental-only limited health service plans.
rules.requires: A claim-status answer must say 'no record of receiving the claim' or give the received date, the insurer claim number and a dated action (in process, denied with reason, paid, suspended with reason, contested with reason). Payment date = EFT posting date, check postmark or documented delivery date. The 30-day clock includes time at the insurer's clearinghouse but not the provider's.
rules.deadline: Applies to every status inquiry; payment-date rule fixes when the 30 days are met.
rules.consequence: A status response without these elements is a regulatory violation that can be cited in a DOI complaint.
rules.provider_use: Use bulk electronic 276/277 status checks; any payer answer lacking received date and dated action is itself a citeable violation. Measure lateness from the clearinghouse acceptance date to the EFT posting date or check postmark.

rules.quote: An insurer may contest a clean claim only in the following instances:
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: A clean claim may be contested only for documented preexisting condition/COB/other insurer primary, a retrospective review, information of fraud, or unpaid premium. When contesting for missing information or COB, give an itemization of 'all new, never-before-provided information' within the 30 days, then pay or deny within 30 calendar days of receiving it. A claim denied for non-receipt of the information may be resubmitted and 'shall not be denied on the basis of timeliness' if resubmitted within the insurer's filing timeframe counted from the denial date.
rules.deadline: Contest notice within 30 days of receipt; decision within 30 calendar days of receiving the requested information; provider has 15 business days to answer before the insurer may deny.
rules.consequence: A pend or contest for any other reason is not permitted; the claim is late and interest runs.
rules.provider_use: For 'pended for review' or repeated records requests, demand the specific 706(1) ground and the itemized list; for COB pends, demand the documentation (806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 5(2) requires it be given on request). Resubmissions after an information denial are protected from timely-filing denials.

rules.quote: the insurer shall identify the specific required health claim attachments in its provider manual or other document that sets forth the procedure for filing claims with the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Required attachments must be listed in the provider manual with 60 days' advance written notice of material changes; claims sent with the listed attachments must be paid or denied within 702 time frames; for a retrospective review needing an unlisted attachment the insurer must ask within the payment time frame, finish within 20 business days of receiving the records, and add 12% (or 730) interest.
rules.deadline: Request within 30 days of receipt; review completed within 20 business days of records; provider must answer within 15 business days or loses interest.
rules.consequence: Interest at 12% a year (or the 730 rate) on retrospectively reviewed claims.
rules.provider_use: Answer records requests within 15 business days (to keep the interest right) and then calendar 20 business days; if the payer misses it, demand payment plus interest citing 706(2)(c).

rules.quote: the insurer shall add the interest payable to the amount of the unpaid claim without the necessity for any claim for that interest to be made by the provider filing the original claim.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Interest on late clean claims accrues from the date payment was due under 702: 12% a year if paid 1-30 days late, 18% if 31-60 days late, 21% if more than 60 days late (the higher rate runs from the due date). 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4: interest = days unpaid after due date / 365 x rate x unpaid amount, paid within 30 days after the claim is paid, with patient, member ID, provider, DOS, amount and claim reference.
rules.deadline: Interest due within 30 days after the claim payment date (806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4(3)).
rules.consequence: Unpaid interest is a further prompt-pay violation subject to KRS 304.99-123 fines; exception only for acts beyond the insurer's control (acts of God, disasters, epidemics, strikes, war, riot, facility disruption). No interest on corrected payments made under 304.17A-708(1) (806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4(4)).
rules.provider_use: Compute interest automatically on every late-paid KY in-scope claim (even cents) and batch a monthly 'interest not paid' demand per payer listing claim, received date, due date, paid date, rate and amount; 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4(3) makes it due 30 days after payment.

rules.quote: A fine of one thousand dollars ($1,000) per day or ten percent (10%) of the unpaid claim amount, whichever is greater, for each day that a clean claim remains unpaid in violation of
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). Subsection (3) expressly reaches Medicaid MCOs, also for KRS 205.522, 205.532-205.536 and 304.17A-515 violations.
rules.requires: The Department 'may assess' the per-day fine; up to $10,000 for willful and knowing violation or a pattern of repeated violations.
rules.deadline: Per day while the clean claim remains unpaid.
rules.consequence: Fines are paid to the state, are discretionary, and the per-day fine applies only if the insurer misses the quarterly compliance test in 304.99-123(2) (95% of clean claims adjudicated on time and 90% of non-denied dollars paid on time).
rules.provider_use: State accurately: 'the Department may assess fines of $1,000 per day or 10% of the unpaid amount per day under KRS 304.99-123'. Pattern evidence (many late claims from the same payer) supports the willful/pattern fine; bundle such claims in one complaint.

rules.quote: An insurer shall not require a provider to appeal errors in payment where the insurer has not paid the claim according to the contracted rate. Miscalculations in payments made by the insurer shall be corrected and paid within thirty (30) calendar days upon the insurer's receipt of documentation from the provider verifying the error.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). Contracted providers (the rule is tied to the contracted rate). Medicaid MCO contracts must also comply (KRS 205.5356(2)(c)3; KRS 205.534(1)(c)).
rules.requires: Underpayments against the contracted rate must be fixed without a formal appeal, within 30 calendar days of receiving the provider's documentation. The insurer need not correct if the provider's request comes more than 24 months after the provider received payment.
rules.deadline: Provider: request within 24 months of receiving the payment. Insurer: correct and pay within 30 calendar days of receipt of documentation.
rules.consequence: Knowing and willful failure to comply is an unfair claims settlement practice (KRS 304.12-230(17)), enforceable by DOI (desist order, civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation under KRS 304.99-020). No 730 interest on corrections made in accordance with 708(1) (806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4(4)).
rules.provider_use: Best lever for rate underpayments: send a payment-correction request (not an appeal) listing each claim, contracted rate, allowed amount and difference; cite 708(1) and 304.12-230(17); refuse any instruction to 'file an appeal' (also KRS 304.17A-726). Track the 24-month window from the payment date.

rules.quote: Except in cases of fraud, an insurer may only retroactively deny reimbursement to a provider during the twenty-four (24) month period after the date that the insurer paid the claim submitted by the provider.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Retroactive denials only within 24 months of the payment date (except fraud), with a written/electronic statement of the basis; for COB retro denials the statement must name the responsible payer and address; the provider then has 12 months from notice (or longer if allowed) to bill that payer, Medicaid or Medicare.
rules.deadline: 24 months from the insurer's payment date; provider's 12 months to rebill after a COB retro denial.
rules.consequence: Knowing and willful violation is an unfair claims settlement practice (KRS 304.12-230(17)).
rules.provider_use: Reject any takeback older than 24 months from the original payment (and any without a stated basis or, for COB, without the other payer's name and address); demand reversal of the offset with a citation to 708(3) and 304.12-230(17).

rules.quote: If a provider files a dispute in accordance with subsection (2) of this section, no recoupment shall be made until the dispute is resolved.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Overpayment notice within 24 months of the payment date with amount, patient name, patient ID, DOS, insurer claim reference and basis (e-mail/fax notice only if the provider agreed in writing in advance); provider may dispute within 30 calendar days of the postmark/electronic delivery date by submitting additional information; disputes must be completed within 30 days through the provider appeals process; recoupments require written documentation at the time of recoupment.
rules.deadline: Insurer: notice within 24 months of payment; dispute decided within 30 days. Provider: dispute within 30 calendar days of the notice postmark/delivery.
rules.consequence: Knowing and willful noncompliance when collecting overpayments is an unfair claims settlement practice (KRS 304.12-230(16)).
rules.provider_use: Calendar a 30-day dispute deadline on every refund request; a timely dispute freezes recoupment. If the payer recoups during a dispute, or the notice lacks the required elements or is older than 24 months, demand reversal citing 714 and 304.12-230(16).

rules.quote: No insurer, assignee of the insurer, or other person, whether acting for himself or another in connection with a health insurance transaction, shall make any claim or seek recovery for reimbursement for any overpayment pursuant to any health insurance contract from any person more than two (2) years after the claim was filed, unless the claim was false or fraudulent.
rules.applies_to: Health insurance contracts subject to Kentucky law (fully insured commercial and, on its words, Medicare supplement); insurers, their assignees and recovery vendors. Application to Medicaid MCO claims not confirmed. Not self-funded ERISA plans (not insurance contracts). Not MA (42 C.F.R. 422.402).
rules.requires: Overpayment recovery must be brought within 2 years of the date the claim was filed, absent a false or fraudulent claim.
rules.deadline: 2 years from the claim filing date (can be shorter than the 24-months-from-payment limit of 304.17A-714).
rules.consequence: A recovery attempt after 2 years violates the Insurance Code (DOI complaint; KRS 304.2-140 fine or license action for willful violation).
rules.provider_use: Check both clocks on every recoupment: 2 years from claim filing (304.14-375) and 24 months from payment (304.17A-708/714); cite whichever expired. Also applies to recovery vendors acting for the insurer.

rules.quote: An insurer shall not request or require a provider to pursue any other course of action regarding the payment of health care claims outside of the provisions set forth in KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). 304.17A-724 extends the prompt-pay sections to 'any entity an insurer contracts with to perform claims processing functions'.
rules.requires: Insurers and their claims vendors must use the statutory prompt-pay process and may not push providers into other courses of action on claim payment.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Violation of the prompt-pay statutes (DOI fines under 304.99-123; complaint).
rules.provider_use: When a payer or its vendor says 'submit a formal appeal' or 'use our dispute form' for a prompt-pay or contracted-rate problem, cite 726 and 708(1); also name delegated vendors as bound by 724.

rules.quote: An insurer or entity shall not reimburse on a discounted fee basis unless the disclosure is provided in the contract with:
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). Networks/PPO leasing arrangements.
rules.requires: Discounts may be taken only if the provider's contract identifies the products and markets the discount applies to (or written consent through a PPO network).
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Violation is an unfair claims settlement practice under Subtitle 12 and subject to Subtitle 99 administrative penalties.
rules.provider_use: For unexplained PPO/network discounts on Kentucky claims, demand the contract clause naming that product/market; absent it, demand the undiscounted amount citing 728.

rules.quote: An insurer shall not require a provider to: (a) Use a claim form that is different than the uniform claim form for the provider type as set out in subsection (1) of this section; (b) Modify the uniform claims form or its content; or (c) Submit additional claims forms.
rules.applies_to: All insurers transacting health insurance in Kentucky (Medicaid MCOs through KRS 205.593(2) and 907 KAR 17:015; KEHP through 18A.225(22)). Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency).
rules.requires: Only the uniform claim form (CMS-1500/837P for physicians) may be required; no extra or modified forms.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: KRS 304.99-125: fine of not less than $100 for each offense; each claim required on a non-conforming form is a separate offense.
rules.provider_use: Push back on payer-specific reconsideration or 'claim submission' forms used as a condition of payment of an original or corrected claim; cite 304.14-135(2) and the $100-per-claim penalty.

rules.quote: The department shall, as part of the market conduct survey of each insurer, audit the insurer to determine compliance with KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730 and KRS 304.14-135 and 304.99-123. Findings shall be made available to the public upon request.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.593(2), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: DOI audits prompt-pay compliance in market conduct exams; the commissioner reports yearly to the legislature on payment practices and enforcement, 'including the number of complaints received and those acted upon'.
rules.deadline: Annual report; quarterly insurer prompt-pay reports due 180 days after quarter end.
rules.consequence: Complaints feed market conduct findings and the public annual report.
rules.provider_use: Letters can note that prompt-pay complaints are reported to the Interim Joint Committee on Banking and Insurance and used in market conduct exams; request the payer's public market conduct findings when building a pattern case.

rules.quote: (6) Not attempting in good faith to effectuate prompt, fair and equitable settlements of claims in which liability has become reasonably clear;
rules.applies_to: Any person in the business of insurance in Kentucky except the insured (304.12-220), including HMOs (KRS 304.38-180(3)). Fully insured plans, Medigap, KEHP. Application to Medicaid MCO claims not confirmed. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Prohibits: failing to acknowledge and act reasonably promptly on claim communications (2); no reasonable standards for prompt investigation (3); refusing to pay without reasonable investigation (4); failing to affirm or deny within a reasonable time (5); bad-faith failure to settle when liability is reasonably clear (6); failing to promptly give a reasonable explanation of the basis for denial (14); knowing and willful violation of 304.17A-714 overpayment rules (16) or 304.17A-708 payment-error/retro-denial rules (17).
rules.deadline: 'Reasonable' time; specific days come from 806 KAR 12:092 (15/30/45-day standards) and 304.17A-708/714.
rules.consequence: DOI enforcement: desist order after KRS 13B hearing (304.12-120); civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation for insurers/HMOs/health service corporations (304.99-020(1)(a)); suspension, revocation or administrative fine for willful violation (304.2-140); criminal fine on conviction (304.99-010). Private suits: KRS 446.070 allows damages for statutory violations; whether a provider (as opposed to an insured) can sue under 304.12-230 was not confirmed.
rules.provider_use: Name the exact subsection the conduct fits (e.g., '(14) no reasonable explanation', '(17) refused to correct a contracted-rate underpayment') and state that the facts will be submitted to the Department of Insurance. Avoid claiming a private right of action unless counsel confirms it.

rules.quote: If an insurer fails to settle a claim within the time prescribed in subsection (1) of this section and the delay was without reasonable foundation, the insured person or health care provider shall be entitled to be reimbursed for his reasonable attorney's fees incurred.
rules.applies_to: Claims under 'any contract of insurance' paid to an insured or health care provider: fully insured health policies and Medicare supplement policies issued in Kentucky. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Pay within 30 days of notice and proof of claim; 12% a year interest on the final settlement after day 30 if no good-faith attempt to settle; attorney's fees for the insured or health care provider when the delay was without reasonable foundation.
rules.deadline: 30 days from notice and proof of claim.
rules.consequence: 12% interest and fee-shifting in favor of the health care provider. 'Without reasonable foundation' = 'no rational relationship between the reasons for the delay or denial of a claim and the policy, certificate, or contract, applicable law, or applicable facts' (806 KAR 12:092 Sec. 1(15)).
rules.provider_use: Strongest Kentucky fee-shifting text that names providers: cite it in Medigap and fully insured demands ('delay without reasonable foundation exposes you to our attorney's fees under KRS 304.12-235(3)'). Whether it stacks with 304.17A-730 interest on health benefit plan claims was not confirmed; do not double-count interest.

rules.quote: The insurer shall acknowledge and respond within fifteen (15) calendar days to any written communications relating to a claim.
rules.applies_to: Life and health insurers including nonprofit health service corporations, 'including agents and third party administrators' (Sec. 1(9)), for policies covering medical services (incl. Medicare supplement). Not workers' compensation. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Respond to written claim communications in 15 calendar days; affirm/deny and offer payment within 30 days of due proof of loss (12% interest; attorney's fees if without reasonable foundation; pay undisputed portions); if unresolved at 30 days send a written explanation of delay, which for assigned health claims must also go to the health care provider, then every 45 days; written denial within 15 calendar days of the determination citing the policy provision; no denial based on undocumented phone calls.
rules.deadline: 15 calendar days (written communications; denial notice); 30 days (payment/delay letter); every 45 days while open.
rules.consequence: Regulation is guidance for the commissioner's investigations and enforcement (Sec. 2(2)); violations support unfair claims settlement findings under 304.12-230. Note: 'claimant' is defined as insured/beneficiary/representative, so applying the 15-day response duty to provider letters is not confirmed.
rules.provider_use: Put a 15-calendar-day response date on every written appeal/correspondence to a Kentucky fully insured or Medigap payer and log non-responses; repeated silence is the 304.12-230(2) pattern to bring to DOI.

rules.quote: The commissioner shall send a copy of the complaint to the entity or individual and the entity or individual shall send a written or electronic message response to the commissioner within fifteen (15) calendar days from the date of the commissioner's letter.
rules.applies_to: All entities engaged in the business of insurance in Kentucky (fully insured plans, HMOs, Medigap, Medicaid MCOs as licensed insurers, licensed administrators). DOI's 07/2024 instructions say matters outside its jurisdiction are referred to the appropriate agency; MA, Medicare, VA and self-funded ERISA claims fall outside Kentucky insurance law (see does_not_apply).
rules.requires: DOI must review and investigate written complaints, forward them, get a response within 15 calendar days and 'make a finding' to the insurer and complainant; every written complaint is recorded with its disposition for at least 5 years, indexed by insurer, and considered before renewing any certificate of authority (304.2-160(4)).
rules.deadline: Insurer response to DOI: 15 calendar days from DOI's letter. DOI says most cases finish within 30 days.
rules.consequence: A finding against the insurer; complaint history weighs on license renewal; DOI may use its full enforcement powers (304.2-165(4)).
rules.provider_use: This is the 'they must answer' lever: a payer that ignores a provider letter still must answer DOI in writing within 15 calendar days. File the Health Care Provider Clean Claim Complaint Form (one per patient, multiple DOS) or a written complaint online/by mail/fax 502-564-6090/e-mail DOI.ConsumerComplaints@ky.gov with the claim, proof of receipt and payer responses.

rules.citation: KDOI Health Care Provider 'Clean Claim' Complaint Form (Rev. 10/19); KDOI complaint instructions (07/2024)
rules.quote: One form per patient. Form may include multiple dates of service for that patient.
rules.applies_to: Providers with unpaid or late clean claims from Kentucky-regulated insurers.
rules.requires: Form asks for provider/KY license, insurer contact, policy and group numbers, DOS, amount, date first sent and method, participation status, acknowledgment, denial, payments and information requests, with copies (original claim, acknowledgment, denial) and the patient's insurance card; 'The use of this form is suggested but not mandatory'. Form lists Consumer Protection and Education Division, P.O. Box 517, Frankfort, KY 40602-0517; the 07/2024 instructions list Consumer Protection Division, 500 Mero Street, 2 SE 11, Frankfort, KY 40601, phone 502-564-6034, fax 502-564-6090, DOI.ConsumerComplaints@ky.gov, and say the 15-day insurer response time 'is strictly enforced'.
rules.deadline: No filing deadline stated; insurer has 15 calendar days to respond to DOI.
rules.consequence: Opens a DOI investigation file against the insurer.
rules.provider_use: Pre-fill this form from claim data for every in-scope Kentucky claim past day 30 (and attach the 999/277CA acceptance as proof of receipt). Confirm the current mailing address by phone because the 2019 form and 2024 instructions differ.

rules.quote: An insurer shall not deny a claim for failure to obtain preauthorization if the preauthorization requirement was not in effect on the date of service on the claim.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.522(1)(m), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)).
rules.requires: Insurer must publish the list of services/codes needing preauthorization with effective dates; no prior-authorization denial if the requirement was not in effect on the DOS; unless the contract says otherwise, supplies routinely used in a preauthorized (or no-preauth-needed) procedure may not be denied as incidental.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Denial is contrary to statute; appeal/DOI complaint; UR complaint under 304.17A-613(8).
rules.provider_use: For 'no authorization' denials, check the payer's posted list history for the DOS and cite 603(4)(c); for supply/tray denials bundled into Mohs or excisions cite 603(6).

rules.quote: The insurer's or private review agent's failure to make a determination and provide written notice within the time frames set forth in this section shall be deemed to be a prior authorization for the health care services or benefits subject to the review.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans of KY-licensed insurers, HMOs and nonprofit health service corporations (e.g., Anthem KY fully insured, UHC and Cigna fully insured KY business), self-insured governmental and church plans, the Kentucky Employees' Health Plan (KRS 18A.225(22)) and, through KRS 205.522(1)(m), every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; contracted and non-contracted providers. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)). Not Medicare supplement (KRS 304.17A-008(2)(f)). Includes private review agents (e.g., delegated UR vendors).
rules.requires: Medical-necessity/experimental denials may be made only by licensed physicians 'of the same or similar specialty and subspecialty, when possible, as the ordering provider'; urgent decisions within 24 hours and nonurgent within 5 days of obtaining necessary information; denial notices must give specific medical and scientific reasons, reviewer title and (for notices to providers) the reviewer's medical license number, and appeal instructions.
rules.deadline: 24 hours (urgent) / 5 days (nonurgent) after necessary information.
rules.consequence: Late or missing notice = deemed prior authorization (except documented circumstances beyond the insurer's control); defective denials support appeal and UR complaints to DOI.
rules.provider_use: Ask for the denying physician's specialty and license number on every medical-necessity denial of Mohs, pathology or radiation; a non-dermatologist reviewer and a notice without license number or specific reasons are citeable defects. Use 607(3) when an authorization request went unanswered.

rules.quote: A utilization review decision shall not retrospectively deny coverage for health care services provided to a covered person when prior approval has been obtained from the insurer or its designee for those services, unless the approval was based upon fraudulent, materially inaccurate, or misrepresented information submitted by the covered person, authorized person, or the provider.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured health benefit plans, self-insured governmental and church plans, KEHP (KRS 18A.225(22)); utilization review by insurers and private review agents. Medicaid MCOs not confirmed (304.17A-611 is not on the KRS 205.522 list). Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Authorized services may not be retrospectively denied on UR grounds absent fraud or materially inaccurate information.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Denial contrary to statute; appeal, DOI complaint, UR complaint.
rules.provider_use: Attach the authorization number to every appeal of a post-service medical-necessity denial of an authorized service and cite 611(1).

rules.quote: The internal appeals process may be initiated by the covered person, an authorized person, or a provider acting on behalf of the covered person.
rules.applies_to: Health benefit plans of insurers (incl. HMOs, short-term plans), KEHP; not Medicaid MCO provider disputes (use KRS 205.534/205.646); Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Internal appeal decisions within 30 days of receipt (3 business days expedited); non-coverage-denial appeals decided by a licensed physician not involved in the denial and, on request, a board-eligible/certified physician in the appropriate specialty; relevant records considered and the provider allowed to add information; decision letter with specific reasons, reviewer licensure (and license number to providers), and external review/DOI instructions. 806 KAR 17:280 Sec. 7(1): insurer must allow at least 60 days after receipt of a denial letter to file.
rules.deadline: Provider/member: at least 60 days from receipt of denial letter (longer if plan allows). Insurer: 30 days (3 business days expedited).
rules.consequence: Failure to decide on time is deemed an adverse benefit determination opening external review (304.17A-619(2)); UR complaint to DOI (304.17A-613(8)).
rules.provider_use: In every Kentucky commercial medical-necessity appeal, expressly request review by a board-certified dermatologist (or Mohs surgeon/dermatopathologist/radiation oncologist) under 617(4)(b), and calendar day 30 for the decision.

rules.quote: The insurer's failure to make a determination or provide a written notice within the time frames set forth in KRS 304.17A-617 shall be deemed to be an adverse benefit determination, other than a coverage denial, by the insurer for the purpose of initiating an external review as set forth in KRS 304.17A-623.
rules.applies_to: Same as KY-27.
rules.requires: Deemed exhaustion of the internal appeal when the insurer misses the 30-day decision deadline.
rules.deadline: Triggered on day 31 after the insurer received the internal appeal.
rules.consequence: External review becomes available immediately (with patient consent); new clinical information resets per 619(1).
rules.provider_use: On day 31 without a decision, send the external review request (with the patient's signed consent and records release) citing 619(2) and 623(3)(b).

rules.quote: A covered person, an authorized person, or a provider acting on behalf of and with the consent of the covered person, may request an external review of an adverse benefit determination, other than a coverage denial,
rules.applies_to: Same as KY-27 (fully insured health benefit plans, KEHP; medical-necessity/experimental determinations only).
rules.requires: External review if: adverse determination other than coverage denial; internal appeal completed or insurer late; enrolled on DOS; course of treatment would cost at least $100 uninsured. Request to the insurer within 60 days of the final internal notice, with written consent for records; $25 fee paid to the IRE (waivable, refunded if the covered person wins); standard decision within 21 calendar days of receiving all information (+14 by agreement); expedited within 24 hours.
rules.deadline: 60 days from notice of the final internal decision (KRS 304.17A-623(4)(a)); IRE 21 calendar days / 24 hours.
rules.consequence: Binding decision (see KY-30).
rules.provider_use: Use for denied Mohs/radiation/pathology medical-necessity claims after internal appeal; get a one-page patient consent and records release at check-in so the practice can file without chasing the patient. Note the DOI consumer guide (2017) says 'four months'; file within 60 days to be safe.

rules.quote: Failure to provide coverage as required by the independent review entity shall also: 1. Subject the insurer to the provisions of KRS 304.99-010 and 304.99-020; and 2. Require the insurer to pay the claim that was the subject of the external review, without need for the covered person or authorized person to further establish a right as to the payment amount.
rules.applies_to: Same as KY-27.
rules.requires: Insurer pays the cost of the external review; IRE decision binding on the insurer, admissible in a civil action and presumed scientifically valid; insurer must report implementation to DOI within 30 days.
rules.deadline: Implementation notice to DOI within 30 days of a decision for the covered person.
rules.consequence: Non-compliance is grounds to suspend/revoke the insurer's license, an unfair claims settlement practice (304.12-230(15)), subject to 304.99-010/-020 penalties, payment of the claim and the insured's attorney's fees.
rules.provider_use: After a favorable IRE decision, send the decision with a 30-day payment demand citing 625(9)-(10); costs the payer the review fee whether it wins or loses, which is leverage to settle before review.

rules.quote: On receipt of a written request for review of a coverage denial from a covered person, authorized person, or provider, the department shall:
rules.applies_to: Coverage denials (service specifically limited or excluded) under fully insured health benefit plans and KEHP.
rules.requires: DOI notifies the insurer, which must answer within 10 business days (coverage on the date, internal appeal exhaustion, the specific limitation/exclusion); DOI decides whether the service is specifically excluded; if not, the insurer must cover it or offer external review.
rules.deadline: Insurer response to DOI: 10 business days.
rules.consequence: If DOI finds the service is not specifically limited or excluded, the insurer must either cover it or afford external review (617(5)(f)2), whether or not the person is still enrolled (617(5)(g)).
rules.provider_use: For 'not covered/excluded' denials that are not real exclusions, a provider can ask DOI directly (2017 DOI guide: Health Policy Utilization Review Branch, Attention: Coverage Denial Coordinator, P.O. Box 517, Frankfort, KY 40602 - confirm current address).

rules.quote: Send a copy of the complaint to the insurer or the private review agent within ten (10) days of receipt of the complaint, and require that any written reply be sent to the commissioner within ten (10) days;
rules.applies_to: Insurers and private review agents doing UR for Kentucky health benefit plans (and Medicaid MCO review agents per KRS 205.536(1)).
rules.requires: Written UR complaints from covered persons, authorized persons or providers go to the insurer within 10 days; reply within 10 days; commissioner makes a recommendation; complaints considered before renewing UR registration; DOI provides copies of a registered insurer's UR policies on provider request. 806 KAR 17:280 Sec. 6: reply must include all related correspondence and corrective actions with timeframes; noncompliance may be penalized under KRS 304.2-140.
rules.deadline: Insurer reply: 10 days.
rules.consequence: Recommendation, corrective action plan, penalties, registration consequences.
rules.provider_use: Use for UR process failures (late decisions, wrong-specialty reviewers, missing license numbers, unreachable lines). Request the payer's filed UR policies from DOI to quote them back.

rules.quote: If an insurer issuing a health benefit plan makes a change to an agreement that changes an existing prior authorization, precertification, notification, or referral program, or changes an edit program or specific edits, the insurer shall provide notice of the change to the participating provider at least fifteen (15) days prior to the change.
rules.applies_to: Insurers offering health benefit plans to participating providers; Medicaid MCOs (KRS 205.522(1)(f) lists 304.17A-235). Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: 90 days' notice of material contract changes (payment decreases; orange envelope for most); 15 days' notice before changes to edits or prior authorization programs; on request, explanation of payment methodology (RVU system, edition, conversion factor) under 304.17A-577(1)(b); fee schedule changes 90 days ahead (304.17A-577(2)).
rules.deadline: 90 days (material change, fee schedules); 15 days (edits/prior authorization).
rules.consequence: The statute sets the notice duties but states no specific remedy for missing notice; missing notice supports a reprocessing demand and a DOI complaint. For most material changes the provider may object within 30 days, triggering a 30-day negotiation (235(5)(a)).
rules.provider_use: When a new edit or rate cut starts denying or reducing claims, demand the dated notice; absent 15/90 days' notice, demand reprocessing of claims since the change. Use 577(1)(b) to force the payer to state its pricing method for Mohs/repair combinations before disputing the amount.

rules.quote: KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730 and KRS 205.593, 304.14-135, and 304.99-123 apply to any provider partnership, health maintenance organization, or other managed care organization under contract with the Department for Medicaid Services
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO; 907 KAR 17:015 Sec. 4(3) applies the payment rules to in-network and out-of-network providers.
rules.requires: Kentucky prompt pay (30-day clean claim rule, acknowledgments, contest limits, 24-month retro limits, overpayment dispute process, 12/18/21% interest) applies to Medicaid MCO claims, plus 42 C.F.R. 447.45/447.46 timeliness (90% of clean claims in 30 days, 99% in 90 days).
rules.deadline: As in KY-03 to KY-13.
rules.consequence: DOI fines under 304.99-123(3); DMS contract penalties (KRS 205.534(6), 205.5356(4)).
rules.provider_use: Cite 205.593(2) plus the specific 304.17A section in every Medicaid MCO letter about late payment, retro denial or recoupment; Medicaid MCO interest is owed at the same 12/18/21% rates.

rules.quote: With regard to any adverse payment or coverage determination, copies of all documents, records, and other information relevant to a determination, including medical necessity criteria and any processes, strategies, or evidentiary standards relied upon, if requested by the provider.
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO.
rules.requires: Free copies of everything relied on (criteria, processes, evidentiary standards) on request, and a written reply detailing all reasons for any adverse payment or coverage determination, telling the provider of that right.
rules.deadline: Not stated in statute.
rules.consequence: Contract fines/sanctions up to termination (205.534(6)); DOI fines (304.99-123(3)).
rules.provider_use: Make every first-level Medicaid MCO appeal also a 205.534(1)(a)3 records request; a payer that cannot produce its criteria has a weak denial.

rules.quote: Any claim that remains unpaid for forty-five (45) days or more after the date the claim is received by the managed care organization and that individually or in the aggregate exceeds two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500);
rules.applies_to: Participating providers of every Kentucky Medicaid MCO.
rules.requires: The MCO must offer an in-person meeting with its representative on any clean claim unpaid in violation of prompt pay, and on claims unpaid 45+ days that individually or in aggregate exceed $2,500.
rules.deadline: Triggered at 45 days unpaid.
rules.consequence: Contract sanctions (205.534(6)).
rules.provider_use: Aggregate small unpaid Medicaid MCO claims per MCO until the $2,500 threshold is passed, then demand the statutory meeting in writing - turns many small claims into one escalation.

rules.quote: The reprocessing shall not require a provider to rebill or resubmit claims to obtain correct payment. A claim shall not be denied for timely filing if the initial claim was timely submitted;
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO.
rules.requires: Reprocess claims incorrectly paid or denied in error under 304.17A-708, without rebilling.
rules.deadline: 304.17A-708(1): 30 calendar days from receipt of documentation of a payment error.
rules.consequence: Contract sanctions; DOI fines; 205.5356(2)(c)3 (contracts on/after 4/14/2026) makes 304.17A-708 compliance a contract term DMS must enforce.
rules.provider_use: Reject Medicaid MCO demands to 'submit a corrected claim' for their own pricing errors, and any timely-filing denial of a resubmission when the first claim was on time.

rules.quote: Allowing a provider to file any grievance or appeal related to the reduction or denial of the claim within one hundred twenty (120) days of confirmed receipt of a notification from the managed care organization that payment for a submitted claim has been reduced or denied;
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO.
rules.requires: Provider appeal window of at least 120 days from confirmed receipt of the reduction/denial notice; disposition within 30 days of filing; payment in full within 30 days after an appeal is resolved in the provider's favor.
rules.deadline: Provider: 120 days from confirmed receipt of the notice. MCO: decide in 30 days; pay in 30 days after a favorable result.
rules.consequence: Failure to decide in 30 days 'shall result in a fine or penalty' under the contract (205.534(1)(d)2.b and (6)); contract penalty table also fines systemic appeal failures.
rules.provider_use: Calendar 120 days from the 835/EOB receipt for Medicaid MCO denials; on day 31 without a decision, write to the MCO and copy DMS citing 205.534(1)(d)2; on day 31 after a win without payment, demand payment citing (d)3 and prompt-pay interest.

rules.quote: Only recoup denied payments or issue a demand for payment from a provider upon the final disposition of the audit, including the appeals process established in KRS 205.646; and
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO conducting provider audits.
rules.requires: Allow at least 30 calendar days to produce records; complete audits within 180 calendar days of initiation (unless the provider delays); recoup only after final disposition including external review; base recoupment on actual overpayment unless the provider agrees to a settlement.
rules.deadline: 30 days (records), 180 days (audit completion).
rules.consequence: Recoupment before final disposition or by extrapolation violates statute; contract sanctions; DOI fines under 304.99-123(3).
rules.provider_use: Demand return of any Medicaid MCO audit takeback made before the external review is finished, and refuse extrapolated amounts.

rules.quote: A provider may submit multiple claims to be appealed in a single external independent third-party review if the provider alleges that a Medicaid managed care organization has implemented a policy or practice that results in the denial, in whole or in part, of those claims.
rules.applies_to: Providers with denied services or claims from any Kentucky Medicaid MCO (contracts entered or renewed on/after 7/1/2016); DOS or request on/after 12/1/2016 (907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 1).
rules.requires: After exhausting the MCO's written internal appeal, the provider 'shall be entitled' to an external independent third-party review; the final internal letter must say rights are exhausted, the entitlement, and the time period and address. 907 KAR 17:035: request to the MCO in writing (electronic, fax or mail) within 60 calendar days of receiving the final decision, listing each issue and why it is wrong, limited to the internal-appeal record; MCO confirms in 5 business days and sends DMS the record in 15 business days; medical necessity reviewed by licensed clinicians, coverage issues by DMS; decision within 30 calendar days (+14 by agreement). Either side may appeal to an administrative hearing within 30 days.
rules.deadline: Provider: 60 calendar days from receipt (fax date, e-delivery date, or postmark + 3 days). Decision: 30 calendar days. Hearing request: 30 days.
rules.consequence: MCO must pay within 60 calendar days after appeal rights are exhausted on a decision against it (907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 5); losing party pays the hearing fee ($600 under 907 KAR 17:040 Sec. 3; statute cap $1,000, one fee for bundled claims); contract penalty #45: $5,000 per occurrence for failing to comply with final decisions on claim disputes (CY2026 Humana contract).
rules.provider_use: Bundle every claim denied under the same MCO policy (e.g., a Mohs modifier or pathology edit) into one external review alleging a 'policy or practice'. Note 907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 3(3) still says one claim per review unless DMS agrees; cite the 2019 statutory text.

rules.quote: The party that receives an adverse final order shall pay a fee of $600 to the department within thirty (30) calendar days of the issuance of the final order.
rules.applies_to: Providers and Kentucky Medicaid MCOs after an external independent third-party review decision.
rules.requires: Hearing request within 30 calendar days of DMS's notice (electronic, fax or mail), limited to the review record; hearing in Frankfort (or by phone if all agree) within 60 days of the request; hearing officer decision within 60 days after the record closes; judicial review under KRS 13B.140-150.
rules.deadline: 30 days to request; hearing within 60 days; decision within 60 days of record close.
rules.consequence: Loser pays $600; final order enforceable; MCO pays within 60 days (907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 5; contract 25.10). Forum note: KRS 205.646(4) (eff. 7/1/2025) sends the appeal to the Office of Administrative Hearings within the Department of Law; the older regulation and the contract name other bodies - the statute controls.
rules.provider_use: The fee-shifting and a $5,000 contract penalty for non-compliance give the MCO a reason to settle after an adverse external review.

rules.quote: A Medicaid managed care organization shall not require a provider to appeal or resubmit any clean claim submitted during the time period between the provider's credentialing application date and the completion of the credentialing process.
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO (contracts entered or renewed on/after 6/29/2023).
rules.requires: Claims become payable from the credentialing application date once credentialing/enrollment is met; no appeal or resubmission may be required for clean claims submitted in the credentialing gap; MCO decides on contracting within 30 days of verified credentialing information and loads the contract within 10 days (+15 with notice).
rules.deadline: 30 days (contract decision); 10 (+15) days (system load).
rules.consequence: DOI fines under 304.99-123(3); contract sanctions (205.534(6)).
rules.provider_use: For new clinicians, bill Medicaid MCO claims from the credentialing application date and demand automatic payment once loaded, citing 205.532(9).

rules.quote: A managed care organization shall maintain an interactive website, operated by the managed care organization, that allows providers to file grievances, appeals, and supporting documentation electronically in an encrypted format that complies with federal law and that allows a provider to review the current status of a matter relating to an appeal or a grievance filed concerning a submitted claim.
rules.applies_to: Every Kentucky Medicaid MCO.
rules.requires: Electronic appeal filing with status tracking; posted name, individual e-mail and phone of provider relations representatives for behavioral health, physical health and contract changes; plain-language appeal and external review process; updates within 30 days.
rules.deadline: Website updates within 30 days of changes.
rules.consequence: Contract sanctions (205.534(6)); DOI fines (304.99-123(3) lists 205.533 by range 205.532-205.536).
rules.provider_use: Use the MCO portal for bulk appeals with status tracking and escalate directly to the named physical-health provider representative by e-mail.

rules.quote: The Department for Medicaid Services shall, in all instances, exercise its rights under a contract with a Medicaid managed care organization to impose all remedies available to the department under the terms of the contract, at law, or equity
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCO contracts entered into, renewed or extended on or after April 14, 2026.
rules.requires: Contracts must require compliance with KRS 304.17A-708 and the 304.17A sections listed in KRS 205.522; DMS must impose remedies for any contract or law violation; penalties go to the MCO compliance fund (205.5357).
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Mandatory DMS remedies for violations.
rules.provider_use: When an MCO violates 304.17A-708 or 205.534, copy DMS and cite 205.5356(4): DMS has no discretion not to act once it finds a violation.

rules.quote: The Department of Insurance shall then make a determination of whether the contract violation was also a violation of KRS 304.17A-700 to 304.17A-730.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCOs.
rules.requires: DMS sends DOI a monthly report of every corrective action plan, fine or sanction for prompt-payment contract violations; DOI decides whether prompt pay was also violated.
rules.deadline: Monthly.
rules.consequence: Double exposure: DMS contract penalties plus DOI fines.
rules.provider_use: Complain to both DMS and DOI on Medicaid MCO payment delays; letters can say the matter will be reported to both agencies.

rules.citation: Kentucky Medicaid MCO contract CY2026, Section 27.2 (Humana; same text in Aetna)
rules.quote: The Contractor shall consider timely claims filing to be within three-hundred sixty-five (365) Days of the date of service.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCO claims (verified in the CY2026 Humana and Aetna contracts posted by DMS; other MCO contracts not read).
rules.requires: 365-day timely filing from DOS; 90% of clean claims paid or denied within 30 days and 99% processed within 90 days; comply with KRS 304.17A-700-730, 205.593, 304.14-135, 304.99-123; in-person meeting rights; reprocess incorrectly paid/denied claims under 304.17A-708 without rebilling, 'no Claim shall be denied for timely filing if the Claim was timely submitted'; date of receipt = MCO date stamp; denial notices must give the reason. Related: retro MCO-change claims may be filed after the timely filing period when the provider learns of the change from a recoupment letter.
rules.deadline: 365 days from DOS (filing); 30/90 days (payment).
rules.consequence: Contract penalty #56: as in KRS 304.99-123 ($1,000 per day or 10% of the unpaid claim, up to $10,000 willful/pattern); #45 $5,000 per occurrence for not complying with final decisions on claim disputes.
rules.provider_use: Set Medicaid MCO filing deadlines at 365 days from DOS (not the shorter numbers in some manuals) and challenge timely-filing denials of resubmitted claims and of claims re-billed after a retroactive MCO change.

rules.citation: Kentucky Medicaid MCO contract CY2026, Section 25.10 (Humana; same text in Aetna)
rules.quote: If the Provider prevails, in whole or in part, the Contractor shall comply with any Final Order within sixty (60) Days unless the Final Order designates a different timeframe.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCO provider grievances and appeals (Humana and Aetna verified).
rules.requires: Separate provider grievance and appeal process covering denials of services, claims, provider payment and contractual issues; appeals decided by a committee of at least three people not involved in the original decision; written resolution received by the provider within 30 days (14-day extension); right to external independent third-party review; no retaliation for appealing.
rules.deadline: 30 days (+14) for the MCO's written resolution; 60 days to comply with a final order.
rules.consequence: Contract penalties: #41 failure to resolve 99% of provider complaints in time (up to $250 per reporting period); #42 systemic appeal failure ($500/day until CAP implemented); #45 $5,000 per occurrence for not complying with final decisions on claim disputes.
rules.provider_use: Ask in appeals that the committee composition be confirmed; when a decision is late, cite both KRS 205.534(1)(d)2 and contract 25.10 and copy DMS.

rules.quote: A provider shall not be an authorized representative of an enrollee without the enrollee's written consent for the specific action that is being appealed or that is the subject of a state fair hearing.
rules.applies_to: Kentucky Medicaid MCO enrollee appeals (service denials) - an alternative route to provider appeals.
rules.requires: Provider may appeal for the enrollee only with written consent specific to that appeal; enrollee has 60 calendar days to appeal; MCO resolves in 30 days (+14); state fair hearing within 120 days of the final MCO letter. 907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 2(4): provider external review is barred if the enrollee already requested a fair hearing on the same claim.
rules.deadline: 60 days (enrollee appeal); 120 days (fair hearing).
rules.consequence: Choosing the enrollee route can block the provider external review on the same claim.
rules.provider_use: Prefer the provider route (205.534 + 205.646) for payment disputes; use the enrollee route only with consent and when the service itself (not payment) is at issue.

rules.quote: Accepting a notice from a Medicare carrier on dually assigned claims submitted by participating physicians and suppliers as a claim for benefits in place of any other claim form required and making a payment determination on the basis of the information contained in that notice;
rules.applies_to: Medicare supplement (Medigap) insurers in Kentucky, for claims of Medicare-participating physicians.
rules.requires: Accept the Medicare crossover notice as the claim, notify the participating physician and beneficiary of the determination, and pay the participating physician.
rules.deadline: Not stated here; KRS 304.12-235 gives 30 days from notice and proof of claim.
rules.consequence: Regulatory violation (DOI complaint); late payment carries 12% interest and possible attorney's fees under KRS 304.12-235.
rules.provider_use: For Medigap balances after Medicare paid, demand payment on the crossover itself, cite 806 KAR 17:570 Sec. 15 and KRS 304.12-235, and refuse requests to resubmit on a separate form.

rules.quote: Following credentialing, the applicant and, upon the applicant's signing of a contract with the managed care plan, the insurer shall make payments to the applicant for services rendered during the credentialing process in accordance with procedures for reimbursement for participating providers.
rules.applies_to: Insurers issuing managed care plans (commercial). Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Credentialing decision within 45 days of a complete CAQH application (except events beyond control); after contracting, services during credentialing paid at participating rates.
rules.deadline: 45 days from complete application.
rules.consequence: Statutory violation (DOI complaint).
rules.provider_use: Hold and later bill commercial claims for new clinicians from the credentialing period and demand in-network payment under 576(3).

rules.quote: It is an unfair trade practice for an insurer that offers multiple health benefit plans to require a health care provider, as a condition of participation in a health benefit plan of the insurer, to participate in any of the insurer's other health benefit plans.
rules.applies_to: Insurers offering multiple health benefit plans in Kentucky.
rules.requires: No all-products clauses (such a contract provision 'is void'); coinsurance must be computed on the amount the provider actually received.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Unfair trade practice; desist order (304.12-120); void contract term.
rules.provider_use: Negotiating leverage: the practice can drop a low-paying product line without losing others.

rules.quote: A person injured by the violation of any statute may recover from the offender such damages as he sustained by reason of the violation, although a penalty or forfeiture is imposed for such violation.
rules.applies_to: Any person injured by a statutory violation (general Kentucky rule).
rules.requires: Creates a damages remedy for statutory violations.
rules.deadline: Limitations period not researched.
rules.consequence: Potential civil damages. Whether a provider (not the insured) can use it with KRS 304.12-230 or 304.17A-700 et seq. against a health insurer was not confirmed (no case law reviewed).
rules.provider_use: Mention litigation only after counsel confirms provider standing; the DOI complaint route is certain, the lawsuit route is not.

rules.quote: Every insurer shall offer a program under which a participating provider may qualify for an exemption from the requirement to obtain prior authorization for any covered health care service that requires prior authorization.
rules.applies_to: Insurers and private review agents for health benefit plans; contracts delivered, entered, renewed, extended or amended on/after 1/1/2028.
rules.requires: Prior authorization exemption ('gold card') program; exemption may not require more than a 93% approval rate; annual evaluation; no prior authorization required for exempt services.
rules.deadline: Annual evaluation at contract renewal; notice within 30 days of evaluation.
rules.consequence: Future lever (2028).
rules.provider_use: Track Mohs/radiation prior-authorization approval rates per payer now to qualify in 2028.

rules.quote: Twenty (20) working days of the receipt of requested medical information where the plan has initiated a retrospective review;
rules.applies_to: Insurers (managed care plans) denying coverage of a treatment, procedure, prior-approval drug or device for an enrollee. Not Medicare Advantage (42 C.F.R. 422.402 preempts state law other than licensing and solvency). Not self-funded ERISA employer plans (KRS 304.17A-005(29); 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B)).
rules.requires: Denial letter must state licensure and title of the decision maker, specific medical and scientific reasons for medical-necessity denials, and appeal instructions (writing requirement, time limits, contact name and phone); timing: 2 working days (preauthorization), 24 hours (hospital preadmission), 20 working days after requested records (retrospective review), 20 working days after review starts (other).
rules.deadline: 20 working days after the insurer receives the requested records in a retrospective review.
rules.consequence: Statutory violation supporting appeal and DOI complaint; no separate penalty stated in the section.
rules.provider_use: After sending records for a post-payment or pre-payment review, calendar 20 working days; a late or reason-less denial is a citeable defect.

batch_and_channel: KRS 205.646(2): one external independent third-party review can carry many Medicaid MCO claims if the provider alleges a 'policy or practice'; appeal of a bundled review is a single hearing with a single fee (205.646(4),(6)). 907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 3(3) (older text) still says one claim per review unless DMS agrees - cite the statute.

907 KAR 17:035 Sec. 2(1)(b)-(c): external review requests may go to the MCO electronically, by fax or by mail; the 60-day count starts on the fax transmission date shown on the fax record (postmark + 3 days if mailed). 907 KAR 17:040 Sec. 1(2)(b): hearing requests also by e-mail, fax or mail.

KRS 205.534(1)(b): the Medicaid MCO in-person meeting right triggers on claims unpaid 45+ days that 'individually or in the aggregate' exceed $2,500 - small claims can be aggregated per MCO into one escalation.

KRS 205.533: every Medicaid MCO must run a website for filing appeals and documents electronically with status tracking, and post named provider relations representatives with individual e-mail and phone.

DOI Health Care Provider 'Clean Claim' Complaint Form: one form per patient but multiple dates of service per form; DOI also takes written complaints online, by mail, by fax (502-564-6090) and by e-mail (DOI.ConsumerComplaints@ky.gov); no verbal complaints. Insurer must answer DOI in 15 calendar days (KRS 304.2-165(2)).

KRS 304.17A-708(1): contracted-rate underpayments are corrected on 'documentation from the provider verifying the error' - no appeal form; a single letter listing many claims with contract rate vs. paid amount fits the text (batching itself is a practice choice, not stated in the statute).

KRS 304.17A-714(1),(2): overpayment disputes are made by 'submitting additional information' within 30 calendar days; notices by e-mail or fax are valid only if the provider agreed in advance in writing - decide deliberately whether to agree, and track postmark dates.
KRS 304.17A-704(4) and 806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 2(2): insurers must offer electronic claim status; use bulk 276/277 checks to document receipt dates and non-adjudication cheaply.

806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4: interest must be paid without request within 30 days of claim payment and identified per claim - an automated monthly per-payer interest audit and one demand letter per payer covers every late-paid claim, however small.
KRS 304.17A-607(2)(j)2: UR decision notices may be sent by e-mail or fax only if the provider agreed in advance in writing.

KRS 304.17A-613(8) and 806 KAR 17:280 Sec. 6: written UR complaints go to DOI (Health and Life Division); external review decisions are reported to DOI.UtilizationReview@ky.gov (806 KAR 17:290 Sec. 3(12)) - whether that mailbox accepts provider complaints is not confirmed.
KRS 205.534(4): DMS forwards Medicaid MCO prompt-pay sanctions to DOI monthly - one complaint to DMS can reach both regulators; copying both is cheap.
does_not_apply: Medicare Advantage (Humana MA, Anthem MA, UHC MA, WellCare/Aetna MA and other MA plans, including KY-licensed HMOs' MA products): 42 C.F.R. 422.402 says the MA standards 'supersede any State law or regulation (other than State licensing laws or State laws relating to plan solvency)'. Kentucky prompt pay, interest, UCSPA, UR and appeal statutes cannot be cited against MA claims; use the federal MA rules (other area).

Self-funded ERISA employer plans (UMR, UHC Shared Services/ASO, Anthem/Cigna/Humana ASO groups): KRS 304.17A-005(29) excludes self-insurers 'exempt from state regulation by ERISA'; 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B) says such plans are not deemed insurers for state insurance law; the DOI appeal guide says these rights do not apply to 'employer self-funded plans'. Use ERISA claims rules instead (other area). KRS 304.9-052 requires anyone acting as an 'administrator' in Kentucky to be licensed; whether that reaches a given self-funded plan's TPA (the definition was not read) and whether it brings any claim rules with it was not confirmed.
UMWA Health & Retirement Funds: if, as appears, these are self-funded multiemployer ERISA plans, Kentucky insurance law does not apply - not verified in this research.
Traditional Medicare (CGS J15), VA Community Care Network (Optum) and TRICARE: federal programs; Kentucky insurance code claim rules do not govern their payments (no Kentucky citation applies).

Medicare supplement: KRS 304.17A prompt pay (700-730) and UR/appeal/external review (600-633) do not apply (KRS 304.17A-005(22)(b)1; 304.17A-008(2)(f)); the DOI guide says appeal rights do not apply to Medicare supplements. Still applicable: KRS 304.12-230, 304.12-235, 304.14-375, 806 KAR 12:092 and 806 KAR 17:570 Sec. 15.

Kentucky Medicaid MCO provider disputes are not 'health benefit plan' disputes (304.17A-005(22)(a)6, (b)12): the commercial internal appeal and external review statutes (304.17A-617, -619, -623, -625) are not on the KRS 205.522 list; use KRS 205.534 and 205.646 instead. Prompt pay still applies through KRS 205.593(2), and 304.17A-600/-603/-607 through 205.522(1)(m).

Commercial external review (KRS 304.17A-623) does not cover pure payment/pricing disputes - 'retrospective review' excludes 'the review of a claim that is limited to an evaluation of reimbursement levels, or adjudication of payment' (304.17A-600(16)(b)) - and does not cover coverage denials (those go to DOI under 304.17A-617(5)); a provider can request it only 'on behalf of and with the consent of the covered person'.

KRS 304.17A-708(1) (no appeal needed, 30-day correction) is tied to 'the contracted rate', so it does not help non-contracted (out-of-network) underpayments; those rely on the plan's benefit terms, 304.12-230 and the internal appeal route.

No interest is owed on corrected payments made in accordance with KRS 304.17A-708(1) (806 KAR 17:360 Sec. 4(4)); 730 interest is excused for acts beyond the insurer's control (epidemics, disasters, strikes, war, facility disruption).

KRS 304.99-123 fines are paid to the state, are discretionary ('may assess'), and the per-day fine applies only if the insurer misses the quarterly 95%/90% compliance test (304.99-123(2)). Letters should not say fines 'will' be imposed.
806 KAR 12:092 is guidance for the commissioner; the regulation itself says it is not intended for private causes of action (Sec. 2(2)).

No Kentucky statute found that sets a minimum commercial timely-filing period for provider claims; the insurer's contract/provider manual controls, subject to 304.17A-706(3)(b) (resubmission after an information denial) and 304.17A-708(3)(d) (12 months to rebill after a COB retro denial). Individual-policy proof-of-loss rules (KRS 304.17-110: 90 days, up to 1 year if not reasonably possible) bind policy forms, and their use by contracted providers was not confirmed.
The 806 KAR 12:095 regulation found first is property and casualty only; the health rule is 806 KAR 12:092.
